Crafter: contrastive actor-critic versus uniform random

Status: completed. Generated 2026-11-07T19:23:38.335409+00:00.

seed 1: 1,000,000/1,000,000 steps (0.46 h, 66/371 contrastive iterations), seed 2: 1,000,000/1,000,000 steps (0.47 h, 68/371 contrastive iterations), seed 3: 1,000,000/1,000,000 steps (0.47 h, 66/370 contrastive iterations)

Each trained policy and its random baseline use the same held-out environment seed list, 64x64 RGB observations, unmodified Crafter rewards, 17 actions, and Crafter's default episode limit of 10,000 steps. The policy sees the last 20 frames through a CNN-LSTM encoder. Actions are sampled, not chosen greedily. Evaluation never updates weights.

Paired mean return difference (contrastive actor-critic minus random): 0.4399999999999998 across 3 completed pairs.

Reference rows come from separate runs evaluated on the same held-out map seeds with the same protocol; they are included for context only.

Hyperparameter overrides: critic_loss_weight = 1.0

Each seed receives equal weight. These are standard deviations, not confidence intervals. Three seeds are a small sample; this experiment does not establish that Crafter is solved or reproduce a published baseline.

Crafter score = exp(mean(log(1 + achievement success percentage))) - 1, over all recorded achievements, including those never achieved. Training curves use the last 100 completed episodes; partial episodes are excluded. Each training iteration collects at least 16 completed episodes from 16 parallel environments, then performs either actor-critic updates or, after 100,000 environment steps and with probability 0.2, contrastive encoder updates. Losses are per-iteration averages over minibatches, not rewards; contrastive loss is only defined on contrastive iterations. The dashed random line is held-out evaluation, not a random training curve.
